recipes.title: Aguachile Verde Ceviche

ingredients.text: 1 1/2–2 lb raw shrimp, cleaned and deveined
1 serrano, or 2 serranos / 1 jalapeño depending on desired spice level

steps: Slice the clean shrimp almost fully down the backside to butterfly-cut it.
Juice the limes and pour the juice over the raw shrimp. Season with salt and pepper.
Set aside for 30 minutes or longer according to preference. The source says it keeps the shrimp in the refrigerator during this step.
After 30 minutes or longer, reserve 1/2 cup of the lime juice for the salsa.
Blend 1/2 cucumber, the peppers, a piece of red onion, cilantro, Jugo Maggi, and the reserved lime juice until smooth.
Add sliced red onion and cucumber to the shrimp. The source specifies removing the cucumber seeds and skin before slicing.
Pour the salsa over the shrimp and vegetables, then mix everything together.
Enjoy immediately or chill in the refrigerator before serving.

recipes.title: Cowboy Butter Lemon Bowtie Chicken with Broccoli

ingredients.text: 1.5 lbs chicken breast or chicken tenders, cut into bite-sized pieces
Salt and black pepper to taste
Salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Boil generously salted water. Cook the bowtie pasta until just al dente. During the last 3 minutes, add the broccoli. Reserve at least 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain the pasta and broccoli together.

Toss the chicken with garlic powder, smoked paprika, onion powder, salt, and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat and sear the chicken in a single layer for 3–4 minutes on the first side and 2–3 minutes on the second, until cooked through to 165°F. Transfer to a plate and leave the browned bits in the skillet.
Reduce the heat to medium. Melt the butter in the same skillet, add the garlic, and cook for 1–2 minutes until golden and fragrant.

Stir in the Dijon mustard and red pepper flakes; cook for 30 seconds. Remove from the heat and add the lemon juice, lemon zest, and a splash of pasta water. Stir until glossy, then return to low heat and season to taste.
Add the pasta and broccoli to the skillet. Toss over medium heat, adding pasta water a splash at a time if needed. Return the chicken to the pan and toss to coat.
Add the parsley and thyme, taste, adjust seasoning, and serve immediately with extra parsley, lemon, and black pepper if desired.
notes: Penne or rotini can replace the farfalle.
The source describes the recipe as taking about 30 minutes, but does not state a serving yield.

recipes.title: Giniling na Baka (Filipino Ground Beef)

ingredients.text: Frozen peas and carrots, to taste (preferred over dicing fresh carrot)
Paprika, amount not shown (visible in video but not listed in the ingredient overlay)
1. Start rice first if serving with rice.
2. Set out 6 bowls: 3 small bowls for garlic, seasonings, and fish sauce; 3 larger bowls for aromatics, potatoes, and trash.
3. Prep vegetables before opening the beef. Dice onion, bell pepper, and potatoes; mince garlic; keep frozen peas and carrots ready.
4. Hold diced potatoes in water if they will sit while you prep or cook. Drain before adding them to the pan.
5. Organize ingredients: onion + bell pepper together, garlic separate, potatoes separate, frozen peas + carrots ready, and seasonings measured nearby.
6. Clean the prep area before handling beef. Clear scraps, wipe the counter, and move prepped vegetables away from the raw meat area.
7. Sweat the aromatics. Heat oil over medium heat, cook onion and bell pepper until softened, 3–5 minutes, then add garlic for 30–60 seconds. Remove to a clean bowl.
8. Brown the beef. Increase heat to medium-high, add ground beef directly from the package to the pan, spread it out, let it brown, then break it up. Drain excess grease if needed.
9. Season the beef with fish sauce, chicken bouillon, salt/pepper, and paprika. Stir well and scrape up browned bits.
10. Add drained potatoes, frozen peas and carrots, then return the onion, bell pepper, and garlic mixture. Stir to combine.
11. Cover and cook until potatoes soften, stirring occasionally. Add a small splash of water if the pan gets too dry.
12. Stir in sugar near the end, taste, and adjust seasoning.
Prep vegetables before opening raw beef to reduce cross-contamination.
Avoid putting raw ground beef on the cutting board; add it straight from the package to the pan.
Wash hands after handling the beef package.
Use a clean spoon for final tasting and serving.

recipes.title: Hailey's Creamy Feta Chicken Pasta

ingredients.text: 1 chicken breast or boneless skin-on chicken thigh
Parsley and chili flakes for garnish

steps: Assemble the bake in a baking dish with the tomatoes, feta, chicken, garlic bulb, sliced onion, bell pepper, and rosemary.

Season the chicken with 1/4 tsp salt and black pepper. Sprinkle Italian seasoning and smoked paprika over the chicken. Season the tomatoes lightly with salt and black pepper. Drizzle olive oil evenly over everything.
Bake at 400°F for 20–22 minutes, or until the chicken reaches 165°F and the tomatoes are soft and bursting.
While the chicken bakes, cook the spaghetti and reserve 1/4 cup pasta water.
Remove the rosemary. Slice the chicken and squeeze out the roasted garlic. Pour in the heavy cream, then mash the tomatoes and feta together until smooth and creamy.
Add the cooked spaghetti and toss until evenly coated. If needed, add a splash of reserved pasta water to loosen the sauce.
Garnish with parsley and chili flakes. Serve immediately.
notes: If the tomatoes taste too tangy, add 1/2 tsp sugar to balance the flavor.
Chicken thighs stay extra juicy, but chicken breast works great too.

recipes.title: Mongolian Beef

ingredients.text: 1 lb beef flank, sliced into 2 inch pieces
1/3 cup cooking oil, for shallow fry
1 tbsp shao xing wine; dry sherry or dry white wine is fine
1 tsp sesame oil, or to taste

steps: Marinate sliced beef with cornstarch, baking soda, shao xing wine, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and white pepper. Mix well and marinate for 15 minutes.
Make the sauce by combining oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, soy sauce, sugar, chicken bouillon, white or black pepper, and sesame oil. Set aside.
Heat a wok with 1/3 cup oil, adjusting the amount if desired. When hot, add marinated beef, spread evenly, and cook 2–3 minutes per side for a crust.
Once beef is about 90% cooked through, strain it from the oil and set aside.
Leave 2–3 tbsp oil in the wok. Add ginger, garlic, and dried chilies. Cook until fragrant.
Add onion and cook 2–3 minutes, until barely translucent.
Add beef back with the sauce and toss evenly for about 2 minutes.
Top with green onions and toss one last time.
Serve with steamed rice or by itself.

ingredients.text: 1 ½ pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs

recipes.title: Air Fried Sweet Potato Cubes

ingredients.text: 1 large sweet potato, peeled or unpeeled
1–2 tsp olive oil or avocado oil
Optional: cinnamon, chili powder, cayenne, or a little honey after cooking

steps: Preheat air fryer to 380°F for 3–5 minutes.
Cut sweet potato into 1/2-inch to 3/4-inch cubes, keeping them similar in size for even cooking.
Toss cubes with oil, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and paprika. Use just enough oil to lightly coat.
Place cubes in a single layer in the air fryer basket.
Air fry at 380°F for 12–16 minutes.
Shake the basket or toss cubes around the 7–8 minute mark.
Check for tenderness. They are done when fork-tender inside and browned/crisp around the edges. Add 2–4 more minutes if needed.
Taste and adjust salt.
Optional finish: parsley, hot honey, lime juice, or a little parmesan.
notes: For larger 1-inch cubes, air fry at 380°F for 18–22 minutes and shake twice.
